findings.reason: the section's whole claim is "one function resolves a lift"; if the function's inputs cannot express the condition it resolves, the node either invents an interface or leaves the reset-anchored path unbuilt.
findings.text: the seam is declared as `effective_budget(config, *, group, reading, now, session)` and the same paragraph says it "takes ... the group's window reading ..., **the clock** and the dispatching session", but no parameter carries the clock; the reset-anchored expiry rule this function must implement is defined per clock (a lift's `ends` names `seven_day`|`five_hour`, `--clock` selects one, and `resets_at` is compared within that clock), and the "fall between two consecutive readings" rule needs the group's reading history since `granted_at`, which a single `reading` input also does not carry — so a node implementing the signature verbatim cannot evaluate the reset-anchored lift the section's done-when requires

findings.reason: `budget.policy` is named as the second reader of the seam, and a config-only function that reads `config["budget"]` directly is exactly the pattern the section says must not remain; the plan must state how the effective block reaches it (a changed signature or a substituted config) or drop it from the reader list.
findings.text: the claim "`budget.policy` and `budget.decide` read it for the resume and coordinator reserves, on routing's path" is only half-true: `budget.decide(state, policy_block, ...)` does take the budget block as an argument, but `budget.policy(config)` takes `config` alone and reads `config["budget"]` internally (`reckon/budget.py:173`), and its routing call site is `budget_module.decide(state, budget_module.policy(config), ...)` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:407`) — so `budget.policy`, like `pace.policy` which the section already concedes "sees only the configuration", has no group, reading, clock or clock to resolve a lift from

findings.reason: the figure is hedged ("about nine hours") and the arithmetic slip below is on the motivating narrative and touches no mechanism, threshold or done-when.
findings.text: the corrected hold length is stated as "about 2026-10-08T13:20Z, nine hours away" from "around 03:12Z", but the section's own figures give ~10 h 08 m between those two stamps (and the releases_at formula at :1944, derived in the same section as "week start plus 0.21/1.1 × 168 h" against a 2026-10-14T05:14:59Z reset, places the release at ~13:20Z)
